comment: Every package served by the repository, in one list.
`deb_pattern` names an asset that the upstream release already publishes;
when it is present the repository serves those exact bytes and never
repackages, so a project that states its own dependencies (pulpit's dlopen
`nfpm` names a template in packaging/ instead, for a project that publishes
only cargo-dist tarballs. The .deb is then built here from the released
binary. Moving a project from the second form to the first is a matter of
deleting its `nfpm` line once its own release workflow grows packaging.
`arches` maps a Debian architecture to the cargo-dist target triple, and
doubles as the list of architectures to attempt. A missing asset is a
skip with a warning, not a failure: upstream may not build that arch yet.
